gloss: Kinkaku-ji, the Temple of the Golden Pavilion in Kyoto

definitions.explanation: A Zen temple in northern Kyoto whose three-story pavilion is covered in gold leaf and stands beside a pond. It was built as a villa by the shogun {足利義満|あしかがよしみつ} at the end of the fourteenth century; its formal name is {鹿苑寺|ろくおんじ}.

examples.english: The present Kinkaku-ji was rebuilt after it burned down in an arson attack in 1950.

notes:
Strictly the name of the pavilion ({金閣|きんかく}), it is used for the whole temple.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {金閣寺|きんかくじ}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{銀閣寺|ぎんかくじ}: the Golden and Silver Pavilions, often visited as a pair
- 「{金閣寺|きんかくじ}」: Mishima Yukio's 1956 novel, based on the 1950 arson

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {銀閣寺|ぎんかくじ}: the Silver Pavilion — built later by {足利義政|あしかがよしまさ}; despite the name it was never covered in silver, and its plain style contrasts with the gold of {金閣寺|きんかくじ}
